text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 alert — elevated packet loss and latency observed from AZB egress into TransitX (upstream ASN 64521). Multiple edge hosts reporting 10-40% loss to 198.51.100.0/24. Paging oncall-net. Root cause suspected: upstream transit path degradation.

oncall-net: I'm up — joining. any prelim dashboards?

sre-alex: Grafana: 5xxs up 3x for AZB region, egress p95 latency 200ms -> 820ms. Backend success rate down ~8% in last 5m.

net-jess: doing quick BGP checks against TransitX peer (192.0.2.1). seeing multiple BGP flaps and increased retransmits.

net-jess: `show ip bgp neighbors 192.0.2.1 received-paths` output shows AS-path growth and intermittent withdraws.

net-jess: running mtr to 198.51.100.12 from azb-egress1:```mtr -r -c 50 198.51.100.12
Start: 2026-03-15 12:03:02
HOST: azb-egress1. LOSS%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
 1.|-- 10.0.0.1     0.0%    50    0.3   0.9   0.2   5.4   1.2
 2.|-- 203.0.113.5 30.0%    50   15.2  22.6  10.1 120.1 34.5
 3.|-- 198.51.100.12 35.0%  50   20.1  30.3  12.2 150.0 40.2```

sre-alex: confirmed packet loss between us and TransitX at their first-hop. Looks upstream, not our internal fabric.

oncall-net: tagging upstream provider ops, will open ticket and request immediate remediation. Also start local mitigations. @net-jess you have the playbook for transit reroute?

net-jess: Yep. Options: 1) advertise less-specific / aggregate via alternate transit (CarrierQ) and shift traffic using local-pref or BGP community; 2) ask TransitX to blackhole/mitigate on their side (slow); 3) apply temporary prepends to make TransitX less preferred. Prefer option 1 + 3 as quick fallback.

eng-miguel: For application-level relief we can increase edge cache TTLs and enable sticky session fallbacks to alternate region while we stabilize. That should reduce cross-region spikes.

support-lina: We need a short customer-facing note if impact expands beyond 10% of requests. Current impact is targeting AZB egress only. Which services are affected?

sre-alex: API and websocket ingress out of AZB are impacted — primarily non-cached endpoints. Looks like ~12% of global user traffic routed via AZB sees errors.

pm-ravi: prepping status page draft. Please confirm severity wording and affected regions.

net-jess: Initiating config change: will prepend TransitX announcements (3x) and at same time raise local-pref for CarrierQ route to prefer it. Applying to AZB edge routers only. Command snippet (FRR):
```
route-map PREPEND_TRANSITX permit 10
 set as-path prepend 64521 64521 64521
neighbor 192.0.2.1 route-map PREPEND_TRANSITX out
route-map PREF_CARRIERQ permit 10
 set local-preference 200
neighbor 198.51.100.5 route-map PREF_CARRIERQ out
```

oncall-net: Apply to a single AZB leaf first (canary) and monitor loss/latency. No global change yet.

net-jess: Canary applied to azb-egress1 at 12:10. Monitoring BGP convergence and traffic shift.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: config-change azb-egress1 applied by net-jess (runbook id: REROUTE-203).

net-jess: Canary results: TransitX path to our IPs shows AS-path with prepends, carrierQ now has increased traffic. MTR to 198.51.100.12 from azb-egress1 now:
```mtr -r -c 50 198.51.100.12
HOST: azb-egress1. LOSS%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
 1.|-- 10.0.0.1     0.0%    50    0.2   0.7   0.1   6.0   0.9
 2.|-- 203.0.113.5  5.0%    50    1.8   2.3   1.1  10.2   1.9
 3.|-- 198.51.100.12 4.0%   50    3.1   4.0   2.0  20.0   3.8```

sre-alex: Good — packet loss down significantly on canary. Proceed to roll for all AZB egress nodes.

oncall-net: Rolling changes to azb-egress2..5. ETA ~6m. Will keep monitoring.

support-lina: Updating status page: "Partial egress packet loss from AZB region impacting API requests. We are routing traffic to an alternate transit provider; mitigation in progress."

pm-ravi: I'll post a short note on customers slack + status page. Keep me posted if we escalate to broader comms.

eng-miguel: Deployed cache TTL bump for non-sensitive endpoints in AZB; should help reduce repeated backend calls.

net-jess: Roll complete at 12:24. TransitX traffic reduced and CarrierQ carrying majority of AZB egress. Current metrics: p95 latency back to ~220ms, 5xxs back to baseline trend, packet loss <3%.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident severity downgraded to P2 — degradation mitigated by reroute.

oncall-net: Opening ticket with TransitX ops (ticket #TX-5481) to get root cause and request fix on their network. Will remove prepends and local-pref once TransitX confirms stable path or network fix deployed.

net-jess: Recording runbook steps and timestamps in the incident doc. Action items: 1) follow up with TransitX and attach BGP dumps 2) coordinate removal of prepends after stable period 3) postmortem within 72h.

sre-alex: Assigning owners: TransitX follow-up -> oncall-net, Postmortem -> eng-miguel + net-jess, Customer comms -> pm-ravi + support-lina.

support-lina: Noted. Drafted longer customer note ready for review.

oncall-net: Thanks team — keeping channel open for the handoff. If TransitX doesn't respond in 30m escalate to carrier ops manager.

pm-ravi: Thanks everyone. Will close paging once TransitX confirms or after 2h of stable metrics.

net-jess: Leaving a final snippet for the post-incident report (BGP snapshot at peak):
```
BGP neighbor 192.0.2.1 Active PfxRcd 120
  Last write 00:01:23, input messages 12345, output 12340
  AS path history: 64521 64599 64599 64521 (flapping)
```

sre-alex: Closing notes: temporary reroute avoided customer-visible outage, postmortem will capture timeline, runbook gaps (faster cross-team comms) and possible automation to detect and auto-shift to alternate transit under defined thresholds.

oncall-net: handing off to follow-up owner. channel clear for now. :white_check_mark:
